correctness.rationale: For a finite n>=3 simple cycle, positive vertex masses and exactly two nonempty color classes, P_m outputs the two normalized class means; across the 2r cross-color edges V(P_m x)=2r|ell(x)|. Zero-sum coefficients c_i give ell(x)=-sum S_i(x_{i+1}-x_i), and cyclic gradient zero-sum duality has sharp norm (max S-min S)/2, attained by a proper arc indicator. Thus K=r(max S-min S). Each of r A-run increments and r B-run decrements is <=range, hence K>=1 and equality iff all normalized run masses are exactly 1/r. Positive masses imply K<r for r>=2, while concentration in an adjacent A/B pair tends to r; mass continuity and connectedness achieve every [1,r). r=1 always gives K=1. Independently brute-enumerated 492 labeled/weight instances and all proper arcs using exact fractions; not an all-n enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Nochetto–Salgado establish TVD for a periodic finite-element interpolant on Cartesian grids, not arbitrary interlaced nonlocal two-cell conditional expectation. Sandryhaila–Moura develop graph Fourier filters. Gaubert–Qu supply general oscillation contraction but do not control the cyclic edge variation of projections. None of these stronger-appearing concepts implies the class-run exact norm.
